discovery: Precision measurement of the cosmic microwave background anisotropies with WMAP, establishing the standard cosmological model
motivation: The Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe, led by Bennett with Page and Spergel as central architects of its instrument and analysis, turned cosmology into a precision science. Its full-sky maps of the microwave background temperature and polarization anisotropies measured the acoustic peak structure with carefully controlled systematics. From these data it determined the age, geometry and composition of the universe to percent-level precision: a spatially flat cosmos made mostly of dark matter and dark energy, seeded by nearly scale-invariant, adiabatic Gaussian fluctuations with a slight red tilt, as inflation predicts, and reionized early. WMAP independently confirmed the dark energy inferred from supernovae and fixed the six-parameter Lambda-CDM model that every later experiment, including Planck, tests. Its predictions for the expansion rate now anchor the most sensitive tests of that model against local measurements, which may point to new physics.
